entry.title: UIFramework v1.9.0: UIFramework v1.9.0 (pre-release)
entry.content:
The Log page's colours can be declared, and what the audit of 2026-11-08 had left open is done. The window's part works with every game as it is. The settings action's part (stub 0.3.0) and the builder's new parts come to a game with its next release; nothing a game has stops working.

Added

  • A game declares the colours of its results on the Log page: .Log(..., styles: new[] { "GAME-OVER|muted", "WIN-*|success" }, outcome: new[] { "DUEL WIN|WIN" }), in the schema log.styles and log.outcome. The colours were guessed from words in the result, so Hangman's GAME-OVER and MISS-LTTR showed in the accent colour. A style is success, warning, muted, accent or none; * stands for any run of characters; the first that fits wins, and a result none names is coloured by its words as before. outcome names what a result is filtered by. See The colours of the results in docs/Schema.md.
  • ask: a field that asks the game whenever it changes (a preset slider whose answer fills other fields) has a name of its own. live on a field that is no button meant the same and is still read.
  • Builder: UiSchema.P(...).AtBottom() (a page at the foot of the rail) and UiWindow.InLanguage("de") (the window's language); both could only be said in the schema. UiHost.Handle takes null for the action's name and uses the one Streamer.bot gives the run.
  • Without the mouse: the rail takes the keyboard (Tab, Up and Down, Enter or Space). In the customise mode the Menu key (or Shift+F10) opens a field's or a page's menu, which has Move up and Move down now, also on Alt+Up and Alt+Down; the moved one keeps the keyboard.
  • A locked window can show the help under the fields: a bulb in its footer, beside the language. The switch for it sits in the customise bar, which a locked window does not have.
  • Tests for the settings action. stub/Stub.cs is compiled into the tests against a stand-in for Streamer.bot and tested there: versions, the download's tries, the files it keeps, how it asks the game.

Fixed

  • The window does not stand still while the game is asked. A Try button, a table and the check before a save waited for the game on the window's own thread, up to 35 seconds when the game's handler hung, and Windows called the window "not responding"; docs/Loader.md said it never froze. The game is asked from another thread now. A Try button's answer and a table's rows arrive when they arrive (the button is greyed, the table says that it is asking); the check before a save waits with the window alive, without input. With every settings action, also the ones games carry today.
  • No answer is not "done". A Try button whose game did not answer (a timeout, a disabled action) showed "done" in green; it says that the game did not answer, in the colour of a failure, and a table says so instead of showing as empty (stub 0.3.0).
  • An import is checked like a save. It wrote values without their fields' limits, without a look at their type and without the game's validate, and it wrote readOnly settings. Every value goes through its field now (a number beyond its limits is pulled into them; text for a number or an option the dropdown lacks is not taken), a readOnly setting is left alone, the dialog names what is not taken and why, and the game checks as before a save. The dialog no longer says "replace": what the file does not name stays.
  • A value the window shows other than the file has it is said: a number beyond its limits or text where a number belongs showed corrected and was written with some later save, without a word, while the game went on reading the file's value. The status line names how many, its tooltip which.
  • A readOnly setting follows its conditions and has its help: showWhen, requires, its section's condition and its help (tooltip or line) were skipped for it.
  • The help under the fields reaches the framework's own fields: the Messages page's sender switches and number format and the Log page's switch kept their help in the tooltip.
  • Long labels and the status line in a narrow window. A switch's label wraps instead of being cut at the window's edge without "…" (German and Spanish labels at the smallest width); the status line takes a line of its own above the footer's buttons when they leave it no room (it read "Ke…").
  • Customise mode: a click on Done or Export right after typing an accent colour is no longer lost (taking the colour rebuilt the window under the pointer); the hint counts the help switch as a change, Reset layout takes it back too and is greyed while there is nothing to take back; an empty accent box opens the picker on the accent in use, not on yellow.
  • Icons: Reset page no longer looks like the mirror image of Reset all and no longer shares its arrow with "read again" on the Log page and the tables; the Log page's folder button has the folder a path field has.
  • twitchOnly works on every field with a label. It was read for switches alone and did nothing elsewhere (three reward ids in Trivia): such a field says "(Twitch only)" in its label.
  • auto brings live and panel. An action without a button followed the typed values only with live and wanted panel although it has a box of its own.
  • Settings action (stub 0.3.0):
    • Closing the update dialog no longer skips the version for good. No skips it, Cancel, the X and Esc mean "not now". Before, No meant "later" and Cancel "skip", so the X skipped.
    • A download GitHub does not deliver is tried three times (a 5xx, a 429, a broken or timed-out connection), and what is left reads "GitHub did not deliver the file ... Try again in a moment" instead of the raw error.
    • Every request to the game has a variable of its own, so a request that hung and answers late cannot be read by the next one; it is unset also when the game's run failed.
    • What holds for the one DLL is kept once: a skipped version and "autoUpdate": false live in <Streamer.bot>\UIFramework\loader.json and hold for every game. They were kept per game, so each game asked again about a version another had skipped. A game's layout file is still read.
    • Today's log lines show while a round runs: the log was opened as a file nobody writes to, which the game's open file is not.
    • One prefix in the log, [<game action>/Settings] or the one the window declares, from the first line to the DLL's lines; it changed to the window's title half-way.
    • The release check counts 1.9 as 1.9.0; the hint for a DLL fetched by hand no longer asks GitHub a second time (offline it stood still again) and does not name a release this settings action is too old for; the dialog no longer says the host block stands "at the end" of the action.

Changed

  • The red i says more: panel, auto or confirm on a field that is no button; placeholders on one that is no message; a platform that is none; a {placeholder} in a message's default text that its list lacks; a page named by its id alone that no setting is on ("mesages"); a custom page behind the generic settings action, which was left out with its fields in silence; a Cmd, Link or Note in the tour and a Tip in a help section (one type in the host block, so the wrong one compiled and was dropped); an unknown style of the Log page's colours. An unknown kind is told the kinds there are, and "The spec overrides" is said in the builder's words.
  • A schema written by hand may use the builder's short forms, which the docs showed as if they were JSON: an option "a|Label", a list column "key|kind|label", shows as "option: key, key", one aliasFactor. A bar segment's colour is read as color too.
  • Texts: English dialog titles in one spelling; the tour names Ctrl+0; the icon hint lists gift and says that an unknown name shows a dot; a page's tooltip in the customise mode names Change icon.
  • Docs: requires greys a field out, showWhen hides it (hide: in front of a requires is still read and no longer recommended); what the game's UiSettings does not know of the conventions; a table of the names a game carries (docs/Getting-Started.md); how a new major line is released (docs/Loader.md).

Removed

  • Code nothing used: Sidecars.Strip, Requirement.Holds(key, op, wanted), Conventions.Aliases() and FrameworkKeys, LayoutFile.OverriddenPages and OverriddenFields, Schema.Defaults() and Aliases(), Text.Or. The tests that went through them go the way the window goes.
  • hosts/rhymetime/spec.json and host-section.cs, left from before the game declared its window.

For 2.0.0

  • The settings action reads its major line from one word, FrameworkLine in stub/Stub.cs, and a test fails while that word and the DLL's major version disagree. Nothing else is prepared in code: what a major version is to take away is listed in PLAN.md.

entry.title: Blackjack Game v17.5.2: A settings action that picks a UIFramework it fits
entry.content:
Fixed

  • The settings action passes over a UIFramework it is too old for. Every game in a Streamer.bot shares the installed UIFramework.dll. Should a later one need a newer settings action than this game's, the action now leaves that file alone and opens the window with an older one that fits, with a line in the log; it used to load whatever was newest. (Settings action 0.2.1.)

Changed

  • The host block is UIFramework 1.8.4's: a setting that holds a number too large for 64 bits is read instead of failing.

entry.title: UIFramework v1.8.4: UIFramework v1.8.4 (pre-release)
entry.content:
Fixed

  • A DLL is not used by a settings action older than it asks for. minHostStub in latest.json only kept such a release from being downloaded; a DLL another game had installed or loaded already was used all the same. The DLL now names the stub it needs (MinHostStub in UIFramework.csproj, in the file's product version as 1.8.4+stub.0.1.0) and opens no window for an older one: the game's dialog says which stub it needs. The release workflow writes the same value into latest.json, so the two cannot disagree.
  • Settings action (stub 0.2.1): an installed DLL that needs a newer stub is passed over for an older one that fits, before it is loaded, with a line in the log. When no installed DLL fits, the dialog says so and offers the download.
  • Log page: lines coming in leave the row being read where it is. The grid kept its offset, which counts rows, and the newest line is the first row: every line a round in chat added pushed the rows down by one. The entry at the top of the grid is found again and put back there. At the very top nothing is held, so new lines show as they come.

Checked

  • A table list's search and the row being edited (the row editor's mistake of 1.8.2): the table does not have it. The row stays while a cell is typed in and on the way to the next cell, and the search takes it when the row is left. One difference stays: saving while the cell is still open ends the row's edit, so a row that no longer matches the search is taken then.

entry.title: UIFramework v1.8.3: UIFramework v1.8.3 (pre-release)
entry.content:
Games need no update.

Changed

  • The accent colour takes a colour's name: red, blue, yellow, any of the colour names WPF knows, in any case (grey spelt either way). The swatch showed such a name already, but the window kept its old accent.
  • The accent colour takes no alpha. #80FF0000 was applied as plain red since 1.8.2; it is not taken any more, and the swatch beside the box stays on the accent in use instead of showing a colour the window does not get. A game's own colour settings keep their alpha.
  • The colour picker opens on a name. With red in the box it started on its default yellow.
  • latest.json lives under its major line. The release workflow wrote every version to lib/v1/latest.json, so a 2.0.0 would have been offered to every v1 game. It now writes lib/v<major>/latest.json: 2.0.0 goes to lib/v2/, which only a stub made for that line reads. The DLL's update check reads the file of its own line.

entry.title: UIFramework v1.8.2: UIFramework v1.8.2 (pre-release)
entry.content:
The second part of the review: the smaller mistakes, the scripts, and the docs and pictures that had fallen behind. Games need no update.

Fixed

  • Customise mode: Show shows a field the game hides. It only took the user's own "hidden" away, and a field hidden in the game's declaration has none; it now writes the "shown" the layout needs.
  • Customise mode: a page dragged down lands after the page it is dropped on. It always went in front, so a page dragged one place down stayed where it was and none could become the last.
  • Customise mode: a field dropped above or below a line the page put together itself (three numbers, two switches) lands above or below the whole line, as docs/Customize.md says, not inside it.
  • Search: a row under a pointer at rest no longer takes the selection from the best match, so Enter goes where the list says.
  • Search finds what the standard pages draw: the sender switches and the number format of the Messages page and the Log page's switch. A tour stop on one of them is no longer dropped.
  • Search: Tab stays in the box while the bar is up, and Esc gives the keyboard back to the field it came from.
  • A list's search leaves the row being typed in where it is. Under the search "app", deleting a "p" from "apple" hid the row under the cursor.
  • Whole numbers show their unit ("Every (min)"), as decimals and durations did; the timer's intervals rely on it. A label that names the unit already stays as it is.
  • A header pill follows the saved value when its switch is not on the window (its page or field hidden in the customise mode); it said "off" for whatever it could not see.
  • The currency note and pill are in the window's language (currency.note, currency.pill; they were English in German and Spanish windows).
  • A condition on a list follows the list: requires: "words" lifts as the first row is added, not after save and reopen.
  • An old name the game lists itself is read the game's way. The conventions' factor on AddictedPayoutCut was applied by the window even where the game listed that name without one, so window and game disagreed (Trivia).
  • Dates in an answer stay text. A table answer or a set value like 2026-11-10T20:15:00 was shown as 11/10/2026 20:15:00.
  • A language text with broken braces is shown as it is instead of keeping the window from opening.
  • Colours: #AARRGGBB, documented all along, is understood by the picker, which opens on the stored colour and keeps its alpha; #abc and F1C40F are read the same by the swatch, the picker and the accent. The accent stays opaque.
  • No rounding noise in saved numbers: a decimal slider at 0.3 and a percent of 35 with a factor are saved as 0.3 and 0.35, not 0.30000000000000004.
  • Log page: a reload keeps the selected line and its detail, and the result filter follows what the log holds now (a log that was empty when the window opened offered "All results" only).
  • Emote pictures: an FFZ emote with a 1x image only has its picture, and a picture that arrives late no longer sits beside another code.
  • Host block: UiSettings.Double reads a whole number beyond long instead of throwing in the game's run.

Changed

  • Tools: conventions-doc.ps1 -Check and check-stub.ps1 notice a change in letter case alone; check-stub.ps1 runs twice in one console; update-host-block.ps1, copy-host-block.ps1, build-import.ps1 and spec-to-window.ps1 take relative paths from where PowerShell stands. New: tools/docs-shots.ps1 renders the screenshots of the docs again.
  • Release workflow: one run per tag (a third tag pushed in a hurry cancelled the second), and build and tests are two steps, so a failed build cannot hide behind passing tests.
  • Docs: every screenshot with the window around it is new (the search is in the header); README names the search, the automation helpers, triggers and methods, and no longer links a deleted file; Schema.md has the timer keys on the Automation page, the real shape of the emotes answer, and says that the game action's Execute Code sub-action needs a name for Execute C# Method (so do Getting-Started and the Help page's note); PLAN.md is of today.
  • hosts/chatgamble, hosts/slotmachine and hosts/rhymetime are what the released games carry and answer.
  • The tests build without analyzer warnings.

entry.title: UIFramework v1.8.1: UIFramework v1.8.1 (pre-release)
entry.content:
The first part of a review of the whole framework: the mistakes a streamer can run into. Games need no update for the window's fixes; the two in the host block reach a game with its next release.

Fixed

  • AltGr no longer counts as Ctrl. AltGr is Ctrl+Alt to Windows, so on a German keyboard { (AltGr+7) jumped to the seventh page of a window instead of being typed, [, ] and } likewise in windows with eight to ten pages; on a Spanish one @ and # went to page two and three. The window's shortcuts (Ctrl+S, Ctrl+F, Ctrl+1 to 0) now take Ctrl without Alt.
  • Typing is left alone by an action that follows the fields. A window with an auto + live action (Trivia's difficulty line) looked at the fields 350 ms after every change, and that look ended the edit of a table cell and turned a half-typed name into a chip (alice,bob became alice, bo, b). It now reads what is there and touches nothing.
  • turnTimeout has no minimum of its own. The conventions' min: 5 went to every game that declared none, so Blackjack's "0 = no limit" was shown as 0 and saved as 5. A game that wants a floor declares it (Battleship does).
  • One game's failed release check no longer silences the update notice. A repository without a published release, a renamed one or GitHub's rate limit kept the notice waiting for good, for every game and for UIFramework itself. Such a game is now left out of that run's notice; only UIFramework's own check (no network) still holds it.
  • A list whose file could not be read cannot be edited. It was not written, as the red i said, but rows could be typed into it and Save answered "Saved". It is greyed out now, with the reason as its tooltip (list.unreadable, in English, German and Spanish).
  • Tip("search") is no mistake. The stop was shown, but the declaration check did not know the part and put a problem behind the red i.
  • The Log page lets go of its folder when the window closes. Its watcher was stopped only when the page was rebuilt; every window closed left one behind, holding the whole closed window, until Streamer.bot ended.
  • A game's own page title comes first. Pg("board", "Rangliste") lost to the conventions' translation of the wording "Board" (the grid, "Spielfeld"), so Hangman's scoreboard page was titled "Spielfeld" in German.
  • The tour leaves Alt+F4 and Alt+Space to the window.
  • Host block: UiTimer.Rearm leaves a timer off that was switched off between its tick and the game's run; before, that run switched the automatic start back on.
  • Host block: the DLL is loaded the way the settings action loads it. For the update notice and UiLive the block used LoadFrom, which refuses a DLL saved from a browser, did not know a folder named v1.8.0, and did not look at the .sha256 beside the DLL. It now uses UnsafeLoadFrom, takes the v, and leaves a DLL alone that no longer matches its hash.
  • Demo game: the Execute Code sub-actions of DemoGame.sb carry their actions' names, so an Execute C# Method sub-action elsewhere can pick them.

Changed

  • docs/Loader.md and docs/Getting-Started.md no longer say that a game action never loads the DLL: it does, for the update notice and the live check, which is also why a framework update is usually used from the next start of Streamer.bot.

entry.title: Trivia Game v9.3.0: An Addicted cut you set, rounds at random times, StartRound (pre-release)
entry.content:
Added

  • The Addicted cut is a setting. Viewers on the addicted list always lost half of every win. Addicted cut under Addicted on the Access page now says how much: 50 as before, 20 for a lighter touch, 0 for none. The message for a viewer added to the list names it as {addictedCut}; one saved with "50%" written out follows the setting too.
  • Rounds while Twitch runs ads. Under Ad breaks on the new Automation page: Start a round when ads start plays as many rounds as fit the ad break, Announce it before the ads says so in chat 1 to 5 minutes ahead, Bonus during ads makes rounds started during a break pay more, and Rounds only during ads keeps viewers' starts to the breaks. Twitch only; the import brings the Ad Run and Upcoming Ad triggers for it, and Trivia: Ad Break Started and Trivia: Ad Break Ended are there for your own actions.
  • An Automation page. The rounds that start themselves moved there from the Game page, next to the ad breaks.
  • Rounds at random times, and only once chat has been talking. Under Rounds that start themselves on the Automation page, Random time draws every wait anew between Every and At most, and Only after chat lines holds a round back until a platform's chat has written that many lines since its last automatic round. Together with the fixed interval these are the three ways a Streamer.bot timer can run.
  • StartRound for your own actions. An Execute C# Method sub-action on the game action starts a round from any action: a hotkey, a Stream Deck button, a raid. Under Ad breaks on the new Automation page: Start a round when ads start starts one with the ad break, as a blitz round if you like; Announce it before the ads says so in chat 1 to 5 minutes ahead; Bonus during ads makes a round started during a break pay more; Rounds only during ads keeps viewers' starts to the breaks. A new section on the Automation page switches on the timed action [HM] - Auto Hangman Timer, which starts a round on every platform you are live on where none is running. It runs the three ways a Streamer.bot timer can: Every so many minutes, at a Random time drawn anew between Every and At most, and Only after chat lines, which holds a round back until a platform's chat has written that many lines since its last automatic round (10 by default). entry.title: Trivia Game v9.2.1: The overlay follows chat
entry.content:
The OBS overlay mirrors what chat is asked again: automatic rounds only go to the platforms you are live on, a chip names the platform a question went to, a &demo=1 left in the source's URL no longer stands in for the game, and the result of a round is shown for its full time before the next question of a run.

Added

  • The overlay names the platform. A chip in front of the question says whether it went to Twitch, YouTube or Kick, for streaming to more than one at once, where every platform plays a question of its own. Which platform it came from under What it shows on the Overlay page turns it off.

Fixed

  • The overlay follows chat even with &demo=1 in its URL. The Try the demo answer told you to add &demo=1 to the OBS source to place it, and an overlay with it never listened to Streamer.bot: it played its three sample questions on their own 10 to 12 second clocks for every stream after, whatever chat was asked. A demo now listens too, and the first real round ends the samples for good. The answer now points to Show a sample round.
  • The overlay's result is shown for its full time in a run. The next question waited for Delay between rounds alone, 5 seconds by default, and cut a 10 second result short. While the overlay is on, it now waits until the result, and the leaderboard after it when that is on, has been up for Result shown for.
  • Automatic rounds only go where you are live. A round was offered to every platform with a connected account, or with Only when chat has been active off to Twitch, YouTube and Kick alike: chats you were not streaming to got questions, and the overlay showed whichever platform's question started last over the one your chat was asked. The timed action now asks each platform first: Twitch through its API with Streamer.bot's own login, YouTube through the broadcasts Streamer.bot monitors, Kick through its public channel page. Where it cannot be told, recent chat decides, as before.
  • The check before saving only asks about what you changed. It named every problem the settings had on every save, so Save & Exit right after a save asked again about something you had already kept on purpose, such as Only when chat has been active switched off. It now asks only about the problems the save brings in.

After importing, save the settings once with the overlay on, so the new overlay page is written to Chat Games\Trivia Game\Overlay. If your OBS source's URL still carries &demo=1, click Set it up in OBS to point it at the plain URL again. Rounds that start themselves now wait until you are live: nothing starts while you are offline.
